title: Mirabel and the Orchard
premise: In 1898, on the pearling coast of a colonial port city, Yara Okafor has spent six years as an indentured clerk for the Meridian Trading Company, hiding her family's unregistered status behind careful silence. When a census taker named Mirabel Hale begins asking pointed questions about the 'Orchard'—the shantytown where Yara's kin live in secret—the company threatens to expose them unless Yara helps falsify records to cover its smuggling debts. As deportation ships are scheduled and the Orchard faces demolition, Yara must decide which single family member can claim the one legitimate berth she can secure, while learning that Mirabel herself is not what she seems. In the end, Yara burns the falsified ledgers, forfeits her own freedom, and gives the berth to her younger brother—only to discover that Mirabel, moved by Yara's sacrifice, quietly registers the whole family under her own name, buying Yara's release at the cost of her career.
about_author: Rafael Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial port records before turning to fiction. His novels examine the paper trails by which empires made people invisible.

chapters.title: Salt and Ink
chapters.summary: Yara Okafor, POV. We meet Yara balancing her clerk duties at Meridian Trading with secret errands to the Orchard, the unregistered settlement where her family hides. She prides herself on being unnoticed. Emotional beat: quiet vigilance, the comfort of routine built on concealment.

chapters.title: The Woman with the Census Book
chapters.summary: Mirabel Hale arrives to conduct the port census, asking questions no official has bothered to ask before. Yara watches her from the counting house window, uneasy. Emotional beat: first tremor of dread beneath ordinary days.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Yara, POV. Mirabel interviews Yara about household rosters and lingers on a name Yara should not know. Yara lies smoothly but realizes Mirabel noticed the lie. Emotional beat: the sick drop of a mask slipping.

chapters.title: The Orchard at Dusk
chapters.summary: Yara visits her mother Adaeze and brother Kofi in the Orchard, warning them about the census. Her uncle Emeka argues they should scatter; her mother refuses to abandon the graves of Yara's father. Emotional beat: love strained between flight and rootedness.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Yara discovers discrepancies in the company books—shipments that never carried pearls—and realizes her supervisor Mr. Calloway expects her to balance them. Emotional beat: complicity closing around her like a net.

chapters.title: Calloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Calloway privately reveals he knows about the Orchard and offers a bargain: help bury the smuggling debts in the census records, or the family's location reaches the authorities. Emotional beat: cold fear dressed as courtesy.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Saw
chapters.summary: POV shift to Mirabel Hale. She is not merely a census taker; she is investigating the trading company for the Colonial Office, using the census as cover. She suspects Yara is both victim and potential witness. Emotional beat: reluctant sympathy hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: A Berth on the Coromandel
chapters.summary: News breaks: the deportation ship Coromandel will carry 'unregistered persons' within three weeks, and only documented passengers may book berths. Yara learns there is exactly one legitimate berth she might secure through company connections. Emotional beat: hope arriving as arithmetic—one seat, many lives.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Family council in the Orchard. Each member argues someone else deserves the berth: Adaeze names Kofi, Kofi names Adaeze, Emeka names no one. Yara cannot bear to choose aloud. Emotional beat: devotion expressed as refusal.

chapters.title: False Entries
chapters.summary: Yara begins forging the ledger entries Calloway demands, hating her own neat handwriting. She copies a key page as insurance without fully admitting why. Emotional beat: self-disgust braided with cunning.

chapters.title: Tea with the Enemy
chapters.summary: Mirabel invites Yara to tea and gently probes her loyalties, revealing she knows the Orchard exists. Yara denies everything; Mirabel lets the denial stand—for now. Emotional beat: two careful women circling, each half-hoping to be trusted.

chapters.title: Kofi's Secret
chapters.summary: Yara discovers sixteen-year-old Kofi has been diving illegally at night to buy his own passage, risking the reefs and the patrols. Emotional beat: fierce pride colliding with terror.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Patrols sweep the Orchard's edge after an anonymous tip—Calloway tightening his grip on Yara. The family scatters to a fisherman's boathouse; Emeka is detained. Emotional beat: the invisible life becoming visible at the worst moment.

chapters.title: Bargaining Chips
chapters.summary: Calloway offers Emeka's release in exchange for Yara destroying Mirabel's collected evidence. Yara pretends to agree, buying time. Emotional beat: loyalty to blood pulling against loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: What Yara Knows
chapters.summary: Yara finally tells Mirabel everything—the smuggling, the forgery, the berth, the tip-off—handing over the copied ledger page. Trust is offered like a wound opened. Emotional beat: relief and exposure in equal measure.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: A monsoon delays the Coromandel by days but also threatens the boathouse. Mirabel warns that Calloway has moved to have Yara arrested for the forged entries. Emotional beat: time collapsing; every door narrowing at once.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: With arrest imminent, Yara must decide who takes the berth. Adaeze secretly signs it over to Kofi, forcing Yara's hand. Yara says goodbye to her mother at the dock fence. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into gift; the choice made by love, not logic.

chapters.title: Fire in the Counting House
chapters.summary: Climax. Rather than surrender the ledgers to Calloway or let him destroy Mirabel's case, Yara burns the falsified books in the counting house, destroying the company's leverage and implicating herself. Calloway is taken by the Colonial Office investigators Mirabel summoned. Emotional beat: ruin embraced as liberation.

chapters.title: Chains and Paper
chapters.summary: Yara sits in a holding cell expecting indenture or worse. Mirabel argues her case, presenting Yara as a coerced witness. Emotional beat: waiting in stillness, courage stripped of any audience.

chapters.title: The Name on the Line
chapters.summary: Resolution begins: Mirabel registers the entire Okafor family under her guardianship, sacrificing her posting and reputation. Yara is released to the Orchard, now provisionally legal. Emotional beat: astonishment at being seen, then saved.

chapters.title: Letters Across Water
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Kofi writes from the far port where his ship landed; Adaeze plants a small orchard behind their newly registered house. Yara takes work keeping honest records for the harbor court. Emotional beat: tender rebuilding, identity chosen rather than hidden.

chapters.title: Mirabel and the Orchard
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Yara's POV. Mirabel, departing on the last boat of the season, asks Yara what she will put in the blank space where 'occupation' once read 'indentured.' Yara answers: 'Free.' The orchard blooms. Emotional beat: belonging earned, truth kept, loyalty redefined.
